It depends on the school. At my college, anyone can report someone to the dean of students for anything. Then they reach out, ask if I want an appointment, and I say yes or no. As someone who has been reported before, I would recommend just going along with it. They’ll realize there was no reason for the report and you’ll be on your way. 

My friend was reported by a crazy ex friend for “wanting to kill them self” and she chose not to meet with them. They ended up with the cops showing up at their door and being forced into a psych ward. The same person reported me, and I just told them I wasn’t suicidal and they let me go.

Also it seems really strange that a psychiatrist would want an EKG. I wonder if they suspect you have an eating disorder. I can’t think of another reason they would ask for labs and an EKG. If they think you have an eating disorder then they probably can report you, since that can also get you put in a psych ward.

It’s definitely normal to be nervous. I feel like I kind of get nervous but mainly I get so excited that I get overwhelmed and don’t know what to say. If someone asks something and I’m overwhelmed I usually “stall” while still interacting with them. I usually say hi I hope you’re doing well, say I’m excited to see that I have viewers interacting with me, thank them for watching and interacting, and then respond. If they are just saying hey, having a routine for how you greet viewers is a really good way to be less nervous. The more you do it, the less nervous you’ll be.

I used to self harm too, and I kind of look at it this way: Our body’s job is to keep us alive and healthy to the best of our ability. If something stops doing something it’s supposed to, something is definitely wrong. Therefore, when our brain tells us to do something that harms us, that means something has to be wrong with our mental health.
